statement: A State or Sub-State must be named as a noun or noun phrase describing a condition of the Data Asset.
rationale: Prevents the lifecycle from mixing conditions with instructions or work steps.
appliesTo: Global State; Sub-State; KA State; KA Sub-State
test: Can the statement “The Data Asset is in [name]” be read as a condition rather than an action?
compliant: Policy; Operating Model; Integrated Design
nonCompliant: Policy; Integrated Design
authority: Normative for this workbook metamodel; not an Editorial Board approval
notes: Plan and Design remain flagged as ambiguous worked-example labels.

statement: Behavioural verbs belong to Activities or Transition names, not State/Sub-State names.
rationale: Separates what data is from what people or systems do to it.
test: Does the label instruct or describe an action? If yes, classify it as Activity or Transition.
compliant: Activity: Policy; Transition: Enter Policy
nonCompliant: Sub-State: Policy
authority: Normative for this workbook metamodel; not an Editorial Board approval
notes: Transition names should use an action verb plus noun-based source/target meaning.

statement: An Activity may preserve the current State; not every Activity causes a State change.
rationale: Avoids falsely promoting every operation into a lifecycle transition.
test: Compare StateBefore and StateAfter. If equal, it is state-preserving.
compliant: Validate while remaining in Integrated Design
nonCompliant: Treat every validation as a transition
authority: Normative for this workbook metamodel; not an Editorial Board approval
notes: Activities may also contribute to later transition readiness.

statement: Permissible activities may occur while the Data Asset remains in the same State or Sub-State.
rationale: Represents repeated, iterative and maintenance behaviour without creating artificial states.
test: Can the activity complete while the source and target State remain identical?
compliant: Review Policy while remaining in Policy
nonCompliant: Create a new State for every review cycle
authority: Normative for this workbook metamodel; not an Editorial Board approval
notes: Use self-transition only where the behaviour is relevant to the state model.

statement: A Sub-State inherits the rules and invariants of its parent Global State and may strengthen but not contradict them.
rationale: Preserves hierarchical state-machine consistency.
test: Do all parent invariants remain true in the Sub-State?
compliant: Policy inherits Plan traceability requirements
nonCompliant: Policy cancels a required Plan invariant
authority: Normative for this workbook metamodel; not an Editorial Board approval
notes: An approved exception is not the same as contradiction.

statement: Global States are fundamental durable lifecycle conditions; Sub-States are more specific conditions within one Global State.
rationale: Keeps the Global Lifecycle small and stable while permitting management detail.
test: Is the condition globally fundamental, or does it specialize a parent condition?
compliant: Design is Global; Logical Design is a Sub-State
nonCompliant: Make every design activity a Global State
authority: Normative for this workbook metamodel; not an Editorial Board approval
notes: Classification must be justified, not assumed from familiarity.

statement: An Entry Condition is a predicate that must be satisfied before a Data Asset may enter a State or Sub-State.
rationale: Defines formal admissibility into a condition.
test: Can the condition be evaluated TRUE/FALSE before entry?
compliant: Required authority exists before entering Design
nonCompliant: “Good design” without an evaluable predicate
authority: Normative for this workbook metamodel; not an Editorial Board approval
notes: Entry satisfaction alone may not authorize a transition.

statement: An Exit Condition is a predicate that must be satisfied before a Data Asset may leave a State or Sub-State.
rationale: Prevents departure merely because activity has stopped.
test: Can the condition be evaluated TRUE/FALSE before exit?
compliant: Required planning evidence exists
nonCompliant: Planning is finished
authority: Normative for this workbook metamodel; not an Editorial Board approval
notes: Exit conditions are source-state predicates.

statement: An Invariant is a predicate that must remain true throughout occupancy of a State or Sub-State.
rationale: Defines what must be preserved while the Data Asset remains in a condition.
test: Must the predicate remain TRUE for the duration of occupancy?
compliant: Material decisions remain traceable in Plan
nonCompliant: Check traceability only at exit
authority: Normative for this workbook metamodel; not an Editorial Board approval
notes: Invariant failure requires a governed response.

statement: A Transition Guard is a predicate controlling whether one specific transition is permissible.
rationale: Allows source, target, governance and KA conditions to constrain movement.
test: Is the predicate tied to a specified source-target transition and evaluable TRUE/FALSE?
compliant: Metadata requirements identified for Plan → Design
nonCompliant: A general aspiration with no transition context
authority: Normative for this workbook metamodel; not an Editorial Board approval
notes: Guards may be contributed by several Knowledge Areas.

statement: A transition is eligible only when applicable source exit conditions, transition guards and target entry conditions are satisfied.
rationale: Creates a formal transition contract.
appliesTo: Transition; Exit Condition; Guard; Entry Condition
test: Exit(Source) AND Guard(Source,Target) AND Entry(Target) all evaluate TRUE.
compliant: Plan exits + KA guards pass + Design entry satisfied
nonCompliant: Move to Design because planning activity stopped
authority: Normative for this workbook metamodel; not an Editorial Board approval
notes: Authorization is assessed separately under IRD-012.

statement: Technical or readiness eligibility does not equal authorization; material transitions require the applicable Decision Right.
rationale: Distinguishes capability/readiness from authority.
test: After eligibility, has an authorized decision holder approved the transition?
compliant: Readiness passes, then authorized role approves Plan → Design
nonCompliant: System moves automatically because all fields are complete
authority: Normative for this workbook metamodel; not an Editorial Board approval
notes: The required authority is context-specific.

statement: Knowledge Areas are not Global Lifecycle States or Sub-States; each may have its own interacting state model.
rationale: Avoids collapsing professional capability domains into data conditions.
appliesTo: Knowledge Area; KA State; Global State; Sub-State
test: Is a KA model represented independently and linked by interaction/guards rather than nested as a Global State?
compliant: Data Quality State contributes a guard to Plan → Design
nonCompliant: Data Quality is a Global Sub-State of Plan
authority: Normative for this workbook metamodel; not an Editorial Board approval
notes: Global Sub-States coordinate applicable KA states.

statement: A Data Asset may simultaneously occupy a Global State and multiple applicable KA States, forming a Composite Data Management State.
rationale: Represents the multidimensional condition of managed data.
appliesTo: Composite State; Global State; KA State
test: Can the record identify one Global condition plus applicable KA dimensions at one point in time?
compliant: Plan.Strategy + Governance State + Metadata State
nonCompliant: Force all KA conditions into one linear lifecycle
authority: Normative for this workbook metamodel; not an Editorial Board approval
notes: Not every KA dimension is applicable in every context.

statement: Applicable KA predicates may constrain Global transitions, including Governance, Metadata, Data Quality, Security, Architecture and Records conditions.
rationale: Makes cross-cutting Knowledge Areas operational rather than decorative.
test: Does each applicable KA contribution resolve to an explicit guard/predicate or documented non-applicability?
compliant: Security classification identified before Plan → Design
nonCompliant: Say Security applies without a testable condition
authority: Normative for this workbook metamodel; not an Editorial Board approval
notes: The relevant KA owns detailed predicate semantics.

statement: The lifecycle may include recursion, branching, return, self-transition and repeated transitions where defined.
rationale: Reflects actual data management rather than a one-way conveyor belt.
test: Are permitted loops and alternate paths explicit and governed?
compliant: Integrated Design returns to Logical Design after conflict
nonCompliant: Assume every Data Asset moves once from left to right
authority: Normative for this workbook metamodel; not an Editorial Board approval
notes: Non-linearity does not remove the need for guards.

statement: An Artefact is produced or modified by Activities; it is not automatically a lifecycle State merely because its name resembles a State.
rationale: Separates deliverables from data conditions.
test: Is the item a deliverable/document/model, or a condition occupied by the Data Asset?
compliant: Conceptual Data Model is an Artefact produced in Conceptual Design
nonCompliant: Conceptual Data Model as a lifecycle State
authority: Normative for this workbook metamodel; not an Editorial Board approval
notes: Strategy, Operating Model and Policy can denote both a condition and an artefact; IDs and context must distinguish them.

statement: An Artefact may provide Evidence when used to demonstrate satisfaction of a condition or control, but Artefact and Evidence remain distinct concepts.
rationale: Preserves audit semantics and reuse of artefacts.
test: Is the item the deliverable itself, or its evidentiary use in a specific assessment?
compliant: Policy artefact provides evidence for Policy readiness
nonCompliant: Treat all documents as evidence without a claim being demonstrated
authority: Normative for this workbook metamodel; not an Editorial Board approval
notes: One artefact may support several evidence claims.

statement: Rules are implemented or evaluated by Controls, and Controls produce Evidence of their operation or outcome.
rationale: Provides an auditable governance chain.
test: Can each important rule be linked to a control and evidence requirement?
compliant: Readiness rule → readiness review → assessment record
nonCompliant: Rule exists with no control or evidence path
authority: Normative for this workbook metamodel; not an Editorial Board approval
notes: The chain may be many-to-many.

statement: An Exception conditionally authorizes deviation from a Rule under defined authority, conditions, duration and evidence; it does not erase the Rule.
rationale: Allows realism without weakening governance.
appliesTo: Exception; Rule; Control; Decision Right; Transition
test: Is the deviation explicitly authorized, bounded and evidenced?
compliant: Approved temporary exception with compensating control
nonCompliant: Ignore an unmet guard because delivery is urgent
authority: Normative for this workbook metamodel; not an Editorial Board approval
notes: Exception expiry/review should be defined where applicable.

statement: A candidate lifecycle element must demonstrate that it represents a meaningful condition before it is accepted as a Global State or Sub-State.
rationale: Prevents designing the metamodel to justify inherited diagram labels.
test: Can identity, persistence, entry, invariants, permissible behaviour, exit and transitions be defined?
compliant: Policy passes a documented state test
nonCompliant: Accept Maintain as a State solely because it appears in an older diagram
authority: Normative for this workbook metamodel; not an Editorial Board approval
notes: Plan and Design remain subject to this test.

shortName: Do not force verbs into lifecycle boxes
statement: Important activities may occur within States or transitions without becoming Global Lifecycle boxes.
rationale: Prevents lifecycle proliferation and conflation of action with condition.
test: Can the verb be represented as permitted behaviour within an existing condition?
compliant: Archive as a transition into an Archived Sub-State, if the model supports it
nonCompliant: Create a Global State for every verb
authority: Normative for this workbook metamodel; not an Editorial Board approval
notes: Final classification of other lifecycle terms remains open.

statement: A simplified reader-facing lifecycle may use accessible labels, but the underlying formal model must retain state semantics, predicates, guards, relationships and traceability.
rationale: Balances usability with rigour.
appliesTo: Diagram; Metadata; State Model; Chapter content
test: Can every simplified visual element be traced to a formal definition and model record?
compliant: Simple Plan → Design visual linked to the metadata workbook
nonCompliant: Publish boxes with no definitions, guards or traceability
authority: Normative for this workbook metamodel; not an Editorial Board approval
notes: Core vs digital-platform placement is an editorial decision.

statement: Plan/Design definitions and worked-example records remain proposed/illustrative unless formally approved by the DMBOK v3 Editorial Board.
rationale: Prevents experimental modelling from being misrepresented as consensus.
test: Does every non-approved record carry the Proposed / illustrative status?
compliant: Plan Sub-State row marked Proposed / illustrative
nonCompliant: Label Plan/Design model as approved DMBOK v3 lifecycle
authority: Normative status-control rule; not an Editorial Board approval
notes: Retained metamodel rules are agreed for this workbook, not necessarily DAMA policy.
